text: ML Drift's GetGpuInfoFromDeviceDescription lowercases the GPU description, sets the vendor by substring match (GetGpuVendor maps 'apple' to GpuVendor::kApple), and for Apple builds AppleInfo from the name and sets supported_wave_sizes to {32}.

ML Drift's AppleInfo::GetGpuFamily (gpu_info.cc) maps A14 and the M1 series to Family::kApple7; A15, A16 and the M2 series to kApple8; A17 Pro, A18, A18 Pro, the M3 series and the M4 series to kApple9; A19, A19 Pro, A20 Pro, the M5 series and M6 to kApple10; A7 to kApple1, and anything else falls through to kApple1.

ML Drift's AppleInfo constructor matches the lowercased Metal device name against a fixed table of names ('apple a7' ... 'apple a20 pro', 'apple m1' ... 'apple m6') by substring, keeping the longest matching key; a name with no match leaves gpu_type = AppleGpu::kUnknown, and GetGpuFamily then returns Family::kApple1 (the family is derived only from the name, not from MTLGPUFamily).

On Metal, ML Drift's CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice (environment.mm) builds GpuInfo from [MTLDevice name] via GetGpuInfoFromDeviceDescription(name, GpuApi::kMetal), then fills MetalInfo from the device: maxThreadsPerThreadgroup, maxBufferLength, the Metal language version from GetMaxSupportedMTLLanguageVersion, and the simdgroup matrix operations.

On the iPhone 17 Pro (iOS 27.0.1, Agello build 2e54fbdb9ca9) the Metal device name is 'Apple A19 Pro GPU' and ML Drift classifies it as family Apple10 (telemetry fact 'Apple A19 Pro GPU, ML Drift family Apple10').

text: ML Drift's AppleInfo::GetComputeUnitsCount returns A14 4, A15 5 (or a value set by SetComputeUnits), A16 5, A17 Pro 6, A18 5, A18 Pro 6, A19 5, A19 Pro 6, A20 Pro 7, M1 8, M2 10, M3 10, M4 10, M5 10, M6 12, unknown 4; the M-series values are commented 'approximate'.
formula: Values read from the switch cases in AppleInfo::GetComputeUnitsCount (gpu_info.cc 863-975); no computation.

text: ML Drift's Metal CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice sets the compute-unit count to 4 when the GPU type is A15 and uname() machine is 'iPhone14,4' or 'iPhone14,5' (iPhone 13 mini and iPhone 13).

ML Drift's Metal CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice registers 8x8x8 FP16 and FP32 wave (simdgroup) matrix operations only when MetalInfo::IsSIMDMatMulSupported (MSL version >= 2.3) and AppleInfo::IsSIMDMatMulSupported (family >= Apple7) are both true, and adds an 8x8x8 BF16 operation when MetalInfo::IsNativeBfloatSupported (MSL >= 3.1 and not is_simulator).
ML Drift's AppleInfo::IsBionic is true for family >= Apple4, and AppleInfo::IsRoundToNearestSupported returns IsBionic(); GpuInfo::IsRoundToNearestSupported uses it for Apple GPUs on non-OpenCL APIs.
ML Drift's AppleInfo::IsSIMDMatMulFp32Perf2x is true for family >= Apple8 or the M1 series; IsGoodTaskSizeForAppleConvSimd lowers its useful-part threshold to 0.6 for F32 precision when it is true.

ML Drift's SupportsConvAppleMPP(gpu_info) is true only for the Metal API on an Apple GPU with AppleInfo family >= Apple10 and Metal language version >= 4.0; SupportsConvolutionInt8 checks it first, and SelectConvolutionInt8 returns ConvAppleMPP when it holds.

ML Drift's metal::GetFastestStorageType returns TensorStorageType::kTexture2D for Apple family Apple1 or Apple2 and kBuffer otherwise; LiteRT's DelegateKernel::GetStorageType uses the backend's fastest type unless the delegate option use_buffer_storage_type forces kBuffer.
ML Drift's Metal CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice sets the 2D image width and height limits to 8192 for Apple1/Apple2 and 16384 otherwise, and image array layers and 3D image dimensions to 2048.

In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork (commit ef08a67858), GetGpuInfoFromDeviceDescription builds AppleInfo from the lowercased value of the environment variable AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU when it is set and non-empty, instead of from the device name; the vendor is still detected from the real device name.

With AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU set, ML Drift's Metal MetalInfo fields still come from the real MTLDevice in CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice (Metal language version, maxThreadsPerThreadgroup, maxBufferLength, is_simulator), because the switch only replaces the name passed to AppleInfo in GetGpuInfoFromDeviceDescription.

In the PowerBeef/LiteRT fork (commit 362759838), the ML Drift delegate's ComputeOptionsFingerprint appends '|agello-simulated-gpu=<value>' when AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU is non-empty, and the weight-cache model identifier uses the backend's serialized-data prefix concatenated with that value.

On the iPhone 17 Pro with AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU='Apple A17 Pro' (Agello build d7fafdca9b7c), the run's telemetry fact reads 'Apple A19 Pro GPU, ML Drift family Apple9': the real device name with the simulated family.

text: ML Drift's metal::Environment constructors call CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice (and so re-read AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU), and InferenceContext::InitFromGpuModel(create_info, gpu_model, id<MTLDevice>, ...) constructs a new Environment for the device on every call.

In the PowerBeef/LiteRT fork, GpuBackendMetal::GetInfo records the telemetry fact 'gpu' as '<Metal device name>, ML Drift family Apple<N>' and reports a kGpuFamilyUnknown anomaly when ML Drift's AppleInfo gpu_type is kUnknown.

ML Drift's GraphFloat32 is a DAG of Node (id, Operation{type string, std::any attributes}) and Value (ValueId, TensorRef<BHWC>, optional QuantizationParams); values without a producer are graph inputs and values without a consumer are outputs.

ML Drift's GpuModel holds input_ids_and_refs, output_ids_and_refs, nodes (GpuNode: unique_ptr<GPUOperation>, input and output ValueIds, name, op_name, optional_tag set, subgraph_id), tensors and const_tensors descriptor maps, and subgraphs.

ML Drift's CreateGpuModelInfo carries precision (CalculationsPrecision), storage_type (TensorStorageType), hints (ModelHints), and caller-provided tensors: predefined descriptors, external_immutable_tensors and external_mutable_tensors, whose ids must not intersect.

ML Drift's CalculationsPrecision has kF32 (F32 data and math), kF16 (F16 data and math) and kF32F16 (F16 data; Convolution, DepthwiseConvolution, FullyConnected and ConvolutionTransposed accumulate in F32); DeduceDataTypeFromPrecision returns kFloat32 for kF32 and kFloat16 otherwise.

In ML Drift's GetTensorDescForValue (gpu_model_util.cc), when the calculation precision is kF16 or kF32F16, every FLOAT32 graph value gets a FLOAT16 tensor descriptor except graph outputs produced by a CAST operation; with kF32 the original data types are kept.

ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::GetConvPrecision returns kF32 for non-FLOAT16 source data, and for FLOAT16 returns kF32F16 when use_f32_accum_for_f16_convolutions is set (precision kF32F16) and kF16 otherwise.

LiteRT's ML Drift Metal delegate (delegate_metal.mm) maps precision kDefault to CalculationsPrecision::kF16 when GpuInfo::IsRoundToNearestSupported() (Apple family >= Apple4) and kF32F16 otherwise, kFp16 to kF16, kFp32 to kF32, and forces kF32F16 when use_f32_accum_for_fp16 is set (LiteRT precision kLiteRtDelegatePrecisionFp16WithFp32Accum).

LiteRT-LM's CreateCompilationOptions (llm_executor_settings_utils.cc) sets the LiteRT GPU precision to kFp32 when the activation data type is FLOAT32 and to kFp16 otherwise; through LiteRT's GetMlDriftPrecision (kFp16 -> kFp16) and the Metal delegate, that gives ML Drift CalculationsPrecision::kF16.
LiteRT's DelegateKernel initialization uses the IrModel pipeline only when options->use_ir_model is set (default false in MlDriftDelegateOptions) and the GraphFloat32 pipeline otherwise.

LiteRT's BuildFinalModel builds the GraphFloat32 from the delegated TFLite nodes (BuildModel) and then calls ML Drift's ApplyGpuModelTransformations; DelegateKernel then applies LiteRT's own litert::ml_drift::ApplyCustomTransformations to the graph.

ML Drift's ApplyGpuModelTransformations runs ApplyCustomTransformations, then general transformations (add_quant_adjustments, remove_degenerate_upsampling, remove_single_input_add, remove_single_input_concat, remove_identity_reshape, merge_consecutive_reshapes, remove_identity_reshape, remove_identity_strided_slice, make_padding_from_concat, make_fully_connected_from_convolution, padding merges, convolution mul/add merges, global_pooling_to_reduce_op), then merge_padding_with_add, returning InternalError if any group fails.

In open-source ML Drift at 15fa9e2, ApplyCustomTransformations (ml_drift/common/default/custom_transformations.cc) returns true without changing the graph, and the model_transformations target picks the 'default' package through mld_platform_alias; LLM-specific graph rewrites in our build come from LiteRT's ApplyCustomTransformations instead.

ML Drift's GraphToGpuModel runs ReserveGraphTensors, creates a GpuModelBuilder with the hints, storage type and use_f32_accum_for_f16_convolutions (precision kF32F16), runs ConvertOperations, adds graph variable_inputs to both input and output id lists, and calls GetGpuModel.

ML Drift's ReserveGraphTensors uploads each constant node's data into its tensor descriptor and accepts only TensorFloat32, TensorFloat16, TensorBool and TensorInt32 constants, failing otherwise with 'Constant node has unsupported tensor type'.

ML Drift's ConvertOperations first calls op_selector.GPUSubgraphFromGraph for each unconsumed non-constant node and, if that fails, op_selector.GPUOperationFromNode; for associative linkable ops it swaps the most recently written input into position 0.

ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::GetGpuModel runs MergeNodes, AssembleCode, ResolveArgs and ExpandSubgraphs, then returns InternalError for any node whose input or output count differs from its GPUOperation's source or destination tensor names.
ML Drift's MergeNodes runs MergeReorderNodes, MergeElementwiseNodes and LinkNodes in that order.

ML Drift's LinkNodes merges a node into its producer only when the producer's first output has exactly one later consumer reading it as input 0, that output is not a model output, the consumer is linkable (elementwise) with one output and all inputs ready, both have the same optional tags and the producer has no subgraph id; MergeGpuNodes names the result 'producer -> consumer'.

ML Drift's OpSelector interface has a pure virtual GPUOperationFromNode and a virtual GPUSubgraphFromGraph that returns UnimplementedError by default; DefaultOpSelector forwards both to ml_drift::GPUOperationFromNode and ml_drift::GPUSubgraphFromGraph.
ML Drift's GPUOperationFromNode sends operation types without a case to SelectDefault, which in the open-source default selector returns UnimplementedError('No selector for <type>').

LiteRT's LiteRtOpSelector (a ml_drift::OpSelector) builds LiteRT custom operation types itself (add values to cache, gated delta update, the Agello bounded attention tail, GLU, QKV norm RoPE, short conv step, RoPE) and passes other nodes to ml_drift::GPUOperationFromNode; its GPUSubgraphFromGraph calls ml_drift::GPUSubgraphFromGraph.
ML Drift's SelectConvolutionApple returns ConvWaveMatrix when SupportsConvWaveMatrix(gpu_info, precision, attr) and IsGoodTaskSizeForAppleConvSimd hold, and ConvGeneric otherwise.

ML Drift's IsGoodTaskSizeForAppleConvSimd uses the GPU's compute-unit count and Apple9-specific thresholds: a useful-part threshold of 0.75 on Apple9 (0.95 otherwise) and a FLOPs-per-thread threshold of 512 on Apple9 (2048 otherwise).

ML Drift's GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize returns 16 on an Apple GPU at CalculationsPrecision kF16 and 8 at kF32F16 or kF32; quantized fully connected builders use it as the largest destination spatial size (token count) that still gets an fc1x1 FullyConnected kernel.
formula: base 4; x2 if precision == kF16; x2 if GPU is not Mali; x2 more only on Adreno gen7+; min(result, 16). Apple kF16: 4*2*2 = 16; Apple kF32F16 or kF32: 4*2 = 8.

text: ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::FullyConnectedInt8ExternalWeights emits an fc1x1_int8_weights FullyConnected node when the destination spatial size is <= GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize or weights are ring-buffered; otherwise, with per-channel quantization, a weight sum, SupportsConvolutionInt8 and no kDisallow8bitConvs hint, it uses FullyConnectedInt8QuantizedWithSrcQuantization; else FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion.
ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::FullyConnectedInt4ExternalWeights applies the same GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize threshold to choose an fc1x1_int4_weights FullyConnected node.

For Gemma 4 E4B (e4b-ours, 8K window) on the Apple M6, the prefill_1024 GPU graph has 1634 nodes including 210 convolution_int8(conv_apple_mpp), 210 quantize_float16_to_int8c4, 23 convolution(conv_apple_mpp) and 23 convolution(conv_apple_mpp) + src softmax nodes; with the simulated A17 Pro, M2 and M1 it has 1424 nodes, 0 conv_apple_mpp and 233 convolution(conv_wave_matrix) plus 23 convolution(conv_wave_matrix) + src softmax nodes.

text: LiteRT's DelegateKernel always adds ModelHints::kAllowSpecialKernels, adds kPreferTextureWeights and kFastTuning when the matching delegate options are on, adds kDisallow8bitConvs when allow_src_quantized_fc_conv_ops is off, and on __APPLE__ copies use_metal_argument_buffers into the hints.
On __APPLE__, LiteRT-LM's CreateCompilationOptions calls SetPreferTextureWeights(false) on the GPU options (true on other platforms).

ML Drift's GetTensorDescForValue switches a value with fewer than 4 channels to TensorStorageType::kSingleTexture2D on Metal (any storage type) when a kSingleTexture2D descriptor can be created for its shape; WebGPU is excluded.

Google's prebuilt v0.18.0 CLiteRTLM.xcframework that Agello ships has 12 defined ML Drift Metal accelerator symbols but 0 Agello telemetry symbols, so none of our ML Drift commits (telemetry hooks, window kernels, the AGELLO_SIMULATE_APPLE_GPU switch) are in what Agello ships.

text: ML Drift's GPUOperation holds generated code (code_), Arguments (args_), a work-group size defaulting to int3(8, 4, 1), a TensorToGrid mapping and a FLOP count; IsLinkable() returns elementwise_.
ML Drift's MakeFullyConnectedExternalWeights checks 'inputs.size() < 2 && inputs.size() > 5', a condition that can never be true, so its 'Expected 2, 3, 4, or 5 inputs' error is never returned.

ML Drift's Metal CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice evaluates IsNativeBfloatSupported (which tests !is_simulator) before it sets metal_info.is_simulator, so the simulator exclusion has no effect when the BF16 wave matrix operation is registered.

ML Drift's Metal inference_context target is an objc_library (Objective-C++), and LiteRT-LM's WORKSPACE comment says ML Drift is declared so the GPU accelerator can be linked statically (//runtime/executor:default_static_gpu_accelerator).

LiteRT-LM's EngineSettings sets AdvancedSettings::allow_src_quantized_fc_conv_ops, when the application left it unset, to true only if the model metadata has an llm_model_type that is not generic (Gemma 4 E4B's metadata has llm_model_type gemma4), and CreateCompilationOptions enables the GPU option when the setting is unset or true; when the option is off, LiteRT's DelegateKernel adds ModelHints::kDisallow8bitConvs, which rules out ML Drift's int8 source-quantized fully connected path.
ML Drift's metal::MetalDevice is a type alias of metal::Environment, which wraps an id<MTLDevice> and its GpuInfo.

ML Drift's metal::Environment constructors build GpuInfo from the device and call xnn_initialize; InferenceContext::InitFromGpuModel(..., id<MTLDevice>, ...) constructs a new Environment per call, and LiteRT's GpuBackendMetalLitert::CreateInferenceContext uses that overload with metal_device()->device().

ML Drift's GetMaxSupportedMTLLanguageVersion returns MSL 2.4 on iOS 15/macOS 12+, 3.2 when the device supports MTLGPUFamilyMetal3 on iOS 18/macOS 15+, and 4.0 when it supports MTLGPUFamily raw value 5002 (Metal 4) on iOS 26/macOS 26+; the 4.0 branch is compiled only when the SDK's maximum allowed OS version is >= 26.

ML Drift's metal::InferenceContext::InitFromGpuModel encodes the GpuModel FlatBuffer if serialization is requested, then runs CopyFromGpuModel, MemoryManager::AllocateMemory, GetMutableNodes, CompileOperations, BindTensorsToOperations, UpdateParams, Tune(TuningType::kFast), resets external mutable tensors to null, finishes serialization, skips the (disabled) ICB block, and (ours) calls DumpGraphForTelemetry('built').

ML Drift's InferenceContext::CompileOperations compiles nodes one after another in a loop on the calling thread (one MSL compilation per node), and Gemma 4 E4B's decode GPU graph (e4b-ours, 8K window) has 1726 nodes on every Apple family measured.

formula: Node count read from the decode row of generated/kernels-by-family.md; one ComputeTask::Compile per node from the loop in CompileOperations.

text: ML Drift's Metal CreateFunction compiles kernel source at run time with [MTLDevice newLibraryWithSource:options:error:], setting the language version to GetMaxSupportedMTLLanguageVersion(device), fast math (MTLMathModeFast and MTLMathFloatingPointFunctionsFast on iOS 18/macOS 15+, else fastMathEnabled) and the defines as preprocessor macros, then newFunctionWithName.

ML Drift's Metal backend builds every compute pipeline from MSL source with newLibraryWithSource in CreateFunction; no code in ML Drift or in LiteRT's ml_drift_delegate at the pins uses MTLBinaryArchive or newLibraryWithData.

In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork (commit 5aaea039f9), InferenceContext::CopyFromGpuModel sets each ComputeTask's label to the GpuNode name, and CreateComputeProgram builds the pipeline from an MTLComputePipelineDescriptor carrying that label when it is non-empty (otherwise newComputePipelineStateWithFunction).

ML Drift's Metal InferenceContext::InitFromGpuModel always calls Tune(TuningType::kFast), and ComputeTask::Tune sets the work-group size to the first entry of GetPossibleDispatches without running or timing any kernel.

ML Drift's Metal GetMetalDefines maps MAIN_FUNCTION to 'kernel void ComputeFunction', __local to threadgroup, __global to device and __constant to constant, so every Metal kernel's entry point is ComputeFunction.

ML Drift's ComputeTask::Compile replaces 8- and 16-wide vector type names (float, half, uint, int, ushort, short, uchar, char) in the generated code with generated '<type><N>_custom' structs before compiling.

ML Drift's metal::MemoryManager::AllocateMemoryForBuffers places all buffer-backed intermediates at offsets in one buffer (kGreedyBySize plan) only when that plan's total is <= the kGreedyBest shared-objects total, <= 128 MiB (kMaxTotalOffsetSizeToEnableOffsetAssignment = 128L * 1024 * 1024) and <= the device's maximum buffer size; otherwise it uses one buffer per shared object.
formula: 128L * 1024 * 1024 = 134,217,728 bytes = 128 MiB (the code's comment says 128 MB).

text: ML Drift's metal::MemoryManager reuses buffers it already owns across models (TakeAvailableBuffer: the smallest existing buffer that fits), allocates a new MTLBuffer only when none fits, and keeps all shared buffers until the manager is destroyed; LiteRT's GpuBackendMetalLitert passes its shared manager to CreateInferenceContext when may_share_memory_manager is set and always to RestoreInferenceContext.

ML Drift's metal::MemoryManager::AllocateMemoryForBuffers uses kConstAlignment 16 only when TARGET_IOS or TARGET_TVOS is defined and 256 otherwise (combined by lcm with the device's linear-texture row alignment); no BUILD or source file in LiteRT-LM, LiteRT or ML Drift at the pins defines TARGET_IOS, so iOS builds use 256.
formula: Branch selection by preprocessor macros; min_common_alignment = lcm(kConstAlignment, row alignment of each texture-backed buffer).

text: ML Drift's Metal backend creates every MTLBuffer with MTLResourceStorageModeShared (Buffer, CreateBuffer, AllocateTensorMemory for kBuffer/kImageBuffer) and standalone textures (kTexture2D, kTexture3D, kTextureArray, kSingleTexture2D) with MTLStorageModePrivate; texture views over buffers take the buffer's storage mode.

ML Drift's metal::MemoryManager treats kBuffer and kImageBuffer tensors, and kTexture2D and kSingleTexture2D tensors on every Apple family except Apple1, as buffer-backed; texture intermediates are assigned with MemoryStrategy::kEquality.

Metal argument buffers are off in our build: ML Drift's ModelHints::use_metal_argument_buffers defaults to false, LiteRT's LrtGetGpuOptionsUseMetalArgumentBuffers returns value_or(false), the Metal delegate forces it false on MTLArgumentBuffersTier1 devices, and LiteRT-LM's runtime does not set the option.

In ML Drift's direct binding mode, MetalArguments::Encode calls setBuffer/setTexture for every resource and passes the packed scalar arguments with setBytes on each encode; in argument-buffer mode the kernel takes 'device ArgBuffer& args[[buffer(0)]]', each ComputeTask allocates an argument buffer of encodedLength, and Encode calls useResource for every resource before binding it at index 0.

ML Drift's InferenceContext::EncodeWithCommandQueue creates DivideRoundUp(nodes, flush_period) command buffers, each with one compute encoder holding up to flush_period kernels, and commits each immediately; EncodeWithCommandBuffer encodes into the caller's command buffer with one encoder per tasks_per_encoder kernels (default 1) and does not commit; both skip nodes whose optional tags are not enabled.

LiteRT's GpuInferenceContextMetal::Dispatch, for every wait type except kGpuDelegateWaitTypeDoNotWait, commits the backend's pending command buffer, calls EncodeWithCommandQueue with kFlushPeriodDuringDispatch = 256, and creates a new command buffer; for DoNotWait it encodes the graph into one command buffer with EncodeWithCommandBuffer.

With LiteRT's flush period of 256, one decode dispatch of Gemma 4 E4B (1726 GPU nodes, e4b-ours, 8K window) encodes 7 command buffers; a prefill_1024 dispatch on the Apple M6 (1634 nodes) also 7; an mtp_drafter dispatch (162 nodes) 1.

sources.detail: node-count table rows decode (1726), prefill_1024 Apple M6 (1634), mtp_drafter (162)

text: ML Drift's Metal path re-encodes every kernel on every dispatch: ComputeTask::Encode sets the pipeline state, binds all arguments and calls dispatchThreadgroups each time, and no recorded command structure is reused because the indirect command buffer path is disabled.

ML Drift's InferenceContext::InitFromGpuModel guards indirect-command-buffer creation with 'bool add_icb_support = false && ...', so no MTLIndirectCommandBuffer is ever built and icb_ stays null; Google's upstream ml-drift 1b18771 has the same guard.

ML Drift's serialized Metal InferenceContext FlatBuffer holds the GpuModel, the tuned work-group size per node, and per node a MetalProgram with the MSL source (code) and define names and expressions; it contains no compiled Metal code.

ML Drift's InferenceContext::RestoreDeserialized verifies the FlatBuffer (DataLossError 'Deserialization failed.' on failure), decodes the GpuModel, allocates memory, recompiles every node from its stored source via DecodeTasks -> ComputeTask::Init -> CompileProgram, sets the stored work-group sizes, binds tensors and updates parameters, and does not call Tune.
ML Drift's serialized GpuNode FlatBuffer table has gpu_op, input_ids, output_ids, name and subgraph_id, but no optional_tag field, so optional-node tags are not serialized.

LiteRT's GpuBackendMetal (constructor with command queue and enable_residency_set) creates an MTLResidencySet on iOS 18/macOS 15+ regardless of the option, but attaches it to the command queue, calls requestResidency and starts a 100 ms requestResidency heartbeat thread only when the option is enabled.

LiteRT's GpuBackendMetal::PopulateResidencySet adds an inference context's constants (AddConstantsToResidencySet) and create_info's external immutable tensors to the residency set and commits it, and BindSpatialTensor adds later-bound tensors; the delegate never calls ML Drift's AddIntermediatesToResidencySet, so intermediate buffers are not in the set.
LiteRT-LM's AdvancedSettings::gpu_enable_metal_residency_set defaults to false, and on __APPLE__ CreateCompilationOptions passes it to GpuOptions::EnableMetalResidencySet.

ML Drift's InferenceContext::Profile collects per-node FLOPs, sizes, shapes and work-group sizes and times kernels in a separate replay (ProfileTimeWithTimestamps, or GetTaskTime on a new command queue as fallback); LiteRT's Metal backend does not call it.

The PowerBeef/ml-drift fork's Metal inference_context target depends on '@agello_telemetry//:metal', a repository that LiteRT-LM agello-next's WORKSPACE declares as local_repository(path = 'agello/telemetry'), so the fork builds only in a workspace that declares @agello_telemetry.

In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork, EncodeWithCommandBuffer and EncodeWithCommandQueue push a debug group named after each node at Agello telemetry level >= 3 (kTrace), use EncodeTimed at level >= 4 (kDeep), and EncodeWithCommandQueue calls agello::telemetry::AttachGpuTiming on each command buffer before committing it.

In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork, InferenceContext::EncodeTimed (telemetry level 4) encodes each kernel in its own compute encoder with stage-boundary timestamp sampling when supported, and a completion handler records each kernel's GPU time in a span named 'gpu.k.<run>:<kernel>' (run: prefill, decode, verify, drafter or other; kernel: the node name with any ' -> ...' tail replaced by ' +fused').

In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork, InferenceContext::DumpGraphForTelemetry writes gpu-graph-<n>-<nodes>-nodes.json into the directory named by AGELLO_TELEMETRY_GRAPH_DIR whenever that variable is set and non-empty, independent of the telemetry level, at the end of InitFromGpuModel ('built') and RestoreDeserialized ('restored'); each node entry has its index, name, work-group size, FLOPs and BHWDC input and output shapes.
conflicts_with: docs/agello/TELEMETRY.md level table lists 'graph dumps' under level 4 (deep); the code ties graph dumps only to AGELLO_TELEMETRY_GRAPH_DIR (TELEMETRY.md's own 'GPU graphs' row says 'any level')

text: ML Drift's Metal host code uses the classic MTLCommandQueue, MTLCommandBuffer and MTLComputeCommandEncoder objects (no MTL4 command objects); Metal 4 features appear only in generated MSL, where ConvAppleMPP includes <MetalPerformancePrimitives/MetalPerformancePrimitives.h> and uses mpp::tensor_ops::matmul2d.
LiteRT's ML Drift Metal delegate takes the command queue from the LiteRT environment option kLiteRtEnvOptionTagMetalCommandQueue and builds its shared GpuBackendMetalLitert with it.
ML Drift's ComputeTask::need_icb_support_ is initialized false and only copied or swapped in the move operations, so CompileProgram never calls CreateComputeProgramWithICBSupport.
ML Drift's ComputeTask move constructor moves the operation, pipeline, MetalArguments, argument-buffer flags, encoder and buffer but not defines_ or label_.
ML Drift's InferenceContext::GetMutableNodes records, for each external mutable tensor id, the nodes that read or write it, and SetTensor uses that map to rebind the tensor on those tasks.
In the PowerBeef/ml-drift fork, NsPerGpuTick computes the GPU timestamp scale once per process (a function-local static) from two sampleTimestamps calls 5 ms apart against a steady clock.

LiteRT-LM's agello::telemetry::AttachGpuTiming counts the command buffer at level >= 1 and adds a completion handler that reports command-buffer errors and, at level >= 2, records the buffer's GPU time against the current run and its kernelStartTime-to-GPUStartTime queue delay.
ML Drift's metal::MemoryManager::AllocateMemory assigns a new model id and allocates external tensors, constant tensors, then buffer-backed and texture intermediates from per-node usage intervals.
ML Drift's README (at 15fa9e2) lists five supported GPU backends: Vulkan, OpenCL (primary for Android), Metal (Apple devices), WebGPU (via Dawn) and OpenGL ES 3.1+.

The open ML Drift tree at 15fa9e2 has backend directories cl/, gl/, metal/ and webgpu/ (README directory structure) and no Vulkan runtime; LiteRT's delegate BUILD depends on @ml_drift//ml_drift/syrtis targets (command_buffer, environment, vulkan_wrapper) that the open tree doesn't contain.
ML Drift's OpenCL ProgramCache can add and export compiled program binaries (AddProgramBinary, GetProgramBinary), read from the driver with CL_PROGRAM_BINARIES in CLProgram::GetBinary.

ML Drift's OpenCL ClOperation::Tune measures candidate work-group sizes on a profiling queue (GetBestWorkGroupIndex) when there is more than one, and the WebGPU InferenceContext tunes with TuningType::kExhaustive unless the kFastTuning hint is set.
ML Drift's OpenGL backend emits GLSL with '#version 320 es' on OpenGL ES 3.2 or later and '#version 310 es' otherwise.

LiteRT's shared_vulkan_env library (ml_drift_delegate/delegate/BUILD) depends on @ml_drift//ml_drift/syrtis:command_buffer, :environment and :vulkan_wrapper; there is no ml_drift/syrtis package in the open ML Drift repository at 15fa9e2, so the Vulkan delegate can't be built from open sources at the pins.

ML Drift's GetGpuVendor maps substrings of the device description to vendors: adreno/qualcomm, apple, mali, powervr/power, advanced micro devices/amd/radeon/xclipse, intel, nvidia/quadro/tesla, maleoon (Huawei), broadcom, lavapipe/llvmpipe.
ML Drift's GpuApi enum has kUnknown, kOpenCl, kMetal, kVulkan, kOpenGl, kWebGpu and kCuda.
ML Drift's GpuInfo::SupportsAcceleratedDp4a returns false for the Metal API and, on __APPLE__ builds, for WebGPU (which runs on Metal there).

LiteRT's ML Drift OpenCL delegate with default precision picks kF32 on old PowerVR Rogue GPUs and kF16 when the CL environment supports it (else kF32); the Vulkan delegate picks kF16 when explicit FP16 is supported; both switch to kF32F16 with use_f32_accum_for_fp16.
